brief.subject: IRS year-end to-dos, Chicago head tax, state wealth-tax fights
brief.headline: IRS Pushes Year-End Prep as Chicago Head Tax and State Wealth Taxes Heat Up
brief.dek: The IRS flags five pre-filing-season steps, Chicago revives a per-employee tax, and Colorado and California tax measures advance.
brief.lede: The IRS wants taxpayers to tackle five items before 2026 ends to ease the coming filing season and avoid April surprises.

sections.heading: IRS Flags Five Year-End Moves
bullets: The IRS is urging taxpayers to act on five items now, before 2026 closes.
Acting early aims to smooth the upcoming filing season and prevent unwelcome surprises in April.
Many year-end payroll mistakes happen well before the final 2026 payroll, so review records now.

sections.heading: Chicago Head Tax Returns
bullets: Mayor Brandon Johnson is again proposing a per-employee corporate tax in his latest Chicago budget plan.
Gov. JB Pritzker repeated his opposition on Thursday, so employers with Chicago staff should watch the budget fight.

sections.heading: State Tax-the-Rich Measures Advance
bullets: Colorado's Supreme Court rejected a bid to void the vote on Amendment 87, a tax hike on top earners.
In California, a billionaire-backed group spent more than $50 million in a week opposing Proposition 40's wealth tax.
High-income owners in both states should track outcomes for their personal tax planning.

sections.heading: Film Credit Eyes Lame-Duck Vote
bullets: A bipartisan coalition is pressing for a federal film tax credit before the 119th Congress ends.
Independent production businesses could benefit if lawmakers act in the remaining weeks.

brief.seo_description: IRS urges five year-end tax steps, Chicago revives a per-employee head tax, and Colorado and California wealth-tax measures move forward.

items.title: Backers of Federal Film Tax Credit Seek Action in Lame-Duck Session
items.snippet: With just weeks to go before the end of the 119th Congress, lawmakers and advocates are making a bipartisan push to get a proposed federal film tax credit over the finish line.

items.title: 5 Key Steps for the 2026 Year-End Payroll Close
items.snippet: The final payroll of 2026 may be weeks away, but many of the mistakes that can complicate year-end have already happened.

items.title: Colorado Supreme Court Rejects Lawsuit Seeking to Stop Income Tax Measure
items.snippet: The Colorado Supreme Court on Friday shot down an attempt to nullify the vote on Amendment 87, allowing the proposal to raise taxes on the state’s wealthiest residents to proceed.

items.title: What Happens When a Long-Term Rental is Sold? The Taxes That Surprise Small Landlords
items.snippet: Documented improvements can lower the gain, if the landlord has the records.

items.title: Deel Unveils Workforce Security Solution
items.snippet: The global payroll and HR platform has launched Deel Security, an end-to-end workforce security solution that detects and prevents identity fraud throughout recruitment and employment globally.

items.title: Billionaires Flood Final Stretch with $50M to Sink Prop. 40, California’s Wealth Tax
items.snippet: A billionaire-backed group fighting Proposition 40 spent more than $50 million over the past week on efforts to thwart the wealth tax.

items.title: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker Again Takes Dim View of Chicago Mayor’s Head Tax Plan
items.snippet: Gov. JB Pritzker on Thursday reiterated his opposition to a per-employee corporate tax in Chicago, as Mayor Brandon Johnson again proposes one as part of his latest city budget pitch.
